evidence: gpt-oss-120b: "# bipartition via BFS coloring" and "color = [-1] * (n + 1)"; the statement says the links admit an assignment where connected elements hold "opposite states"
affordance_in_statement: The system's architecture guarantees that there exists a valid assignment of a boolean state (True or False) to each element such that for every link, the two connected elements hold opposite states.
secondary_shortcut_name: arbitrary subset of a valid independent set
removal_suggestion: Do not guarantee bipartiteness; allow link sets containing odd cycles, or otherwise replace the opposite-state guarantee with a condition that does not provide a two-color partition. This is the only effective removal, although it changes the underlying computational problem because bipartiteness is intrinsic to the current task.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: BFS-color the graph and use color classes (with component-wise choices) as independent sets; take k vertices whenever the attainable independent-set size is at least k.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The graph is guaranteed to admit opposite boolean states across every link.

common_affordance: The explicit guarantee that the graph is bipartite, allowing a BFS two-coloring whose color classes are mutually disconnected

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its approach accumulates global color groups and does not correctly exploit independent choices of the two sides in separate connected components, so it can reject or construct incorrectly when the optimal set mixes sides across components.
The line `color[start]` only accesses the dictionary and does not assign a color, causing a missing-key failure when an unvisited start vertex is processed.
The implementation crashes during its color/order bookkeeping; the shown code initializes color with a sentinel inconsistent with the later component-coloring logic.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit opposite-state guarantee with instances that may contain odd cycles. This removes the universal BFS-color-class shortcut that the surviving model relies on.
